existing_assets.turbo: GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0/4_0/2_0 — implemented in kv-cache, graph, CUDA, Vulkan

axes.axis_1: quant_caps — semantic capability table replacing 27 hardcoded type checks in kv-cache + graph
axes.axis_2: gpu_prober — CMake-time auto-detection using existing llama_prober.py + runtime backend quant registration
axes.axis_3: cpu_fallback — automatic dequant→F16→compute→requant when no GPU kernel exists for a quant type
axes.axis_4: model_modular — selective model compilation via CMake whitelist/blacklist
axes.axis_5: hybrid_uma — heterogeneous CPU+iGPU backend exploiting Unified Memory Architecture for edge devices (cactus-kernels philosophy: zero-copy UMA tensor slicing, Vulkan subgroup dequant, adaptive thermal balancing)

builder_instructions.overview: 5 independent axes implemented in parallel-capable phases. Each phase is self-contained: build, verify, commit. The prober (axis 2) and quant caps (axis 1) have zero dependencies on each other. Backend registration (axis 2 cont.) depends on caps existing. CPU fallback (axis 3) depends on registration. Model modularity (axis 4) is fully independent. The hybrid UMA backend (axis 5) depends on backend registration (phase 3) and quant caps (phase 2) but is independent of the kv-cache/graph refactoring.

phases.name: prober_cmake_integration
phases.description: Wire the existing llama_prober.py into CMake so that 'cmake -B build' auto-detects GPU backends with zero flags. Manual override still works (-DGGML_CUDA=OFF).
phases.principle: The prober already works (llama_prober.py outputs cmake flags). This phase just integrates it into the CMake configure step. The key: only run auto-detection if the user hasn't explicitly set ANY backend flag.

create.description: CMake module that runs the prober and sets cache variables
create.content:
# Auto-detect GPU backends using llama_prober.py
# Included from top-level CMakeLists.txt
# Override: -DGGML_AUTO_PROBE=OFF to disable entirely

option(GGML_AUTO_PROBE "Auto-detect GPU backends via llama_prober.py" ON)

if(GGML_AUTO_PROBE)
    # Check if user explicitly set any backend
    set(_explicit_backend FALSE)
    foreach(_backend CUDA METAL HIP HIPBLAS SYCL VULKAN BLAS MUSA CANN OPENVINO OPENCL)
        if(DEFINED GGML_${_backend})
            set(_explicit_backend TRUE)
            message(STATUS "GPU auto-probe: skipped (GGML_${_backend} explicitly set)")
            break()
        endif()
    endforeach()

    if(NOT _explicit_backend)
        find_program(PYTHON3_PROBE python3)
        if(PYTHON3_PROBE)
            execute_process(
                COMMAND ${PYTHON3_PROBE} ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/llama_prober.py
                WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}
                OUTPUT_VARIABLE _probe_output
                RESULT_VARIABLE _probe_result
                OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
            )
            if(_probe_result EQUAL 0 AND _probe_output)
                message(STATUS "GPU auto-probe result: ${_probe_output}")
                separate_arguments(_probe_args UNIX_COMMAND "${_probe_output}")
                foreach(_arg ${_probe_args})
                    if(_arg MATCHES "^-D(GGML_[A-Z]+)=ON$")
                        set(${CMAKE_MATCH_1} ON CACHE BOOL "Auto-detected by gpu-prober" FORCE)
                    elseif(_arg MATCHES "^-D(GGML_[A-Z]+)=OFF$")
                        set(${CMAKE_MATCH_1} OFF CACHE BOOL "Auto-detected by gpu-prober" FORCE)
                    endif()
                endforeach()
            else()
                message(STATUS "GPU auto-probe: no GPUs detected, CPU-only build")
            endif()
        else()
            message(WARNING "GPU auto-probe: python3 not found, skipping")
        endif()
    endif()
endif()

modify.code_to_add_after_detection:
if detected and probe.get('sdk_commands'):
    sdk_ok = False
    for sdk_cmd in probe['sdk_commands']:

phases.name: cpu_fallback
phases.description: When a quant type has no GPU kernel on the active backend, automatically fall back to CPU dequantization. The user doesn't need to know — it just works, slower.
phases.principle: The fallback is transparent. When the scheduler encounters a quantized tensor type that the backend doesn't support natively, it inserts a dequant→F32/F16 conversion node. The computation happens in F16 on GPU, then the result is requantized (for KV cache writes) or discarded (for attention reads).

mechanism.step_1_detect: At context creation (llama-context.cpp), check: ggml_backend_supports_quant(dev, params.type_k). If false and caps->cpu_fallback_ok, log a warning and set a flag 'k_cpu_fallback = true'.
mechanism.step_2_prefill: If k_cpu_fallback: allocate K as F16 (not quantized). After prefill, quantize on CPU using type_traits->from_float_ref. Upload quantized tensor to GPU. OR: keep K as F16 (simpler, uses more VRAM).
mechanism.step_3_decode: For each new K token during decode: compute in F32 on GPU, dequant existing K cache to F16 on CPU, upload F16 K to GPU, compute attention in F16, discard. This is the same path as the deferred allocation in Phase 9.
mechanism.step_4_reporting: At startup, print which quant types are GPU-accelerated and which use CPU fallback. Example: 'type_k=planar3_0: CPU fallback (no CUDA kernel), type_v=f16: native CUDA'.

phases.name: model_modularity
phases.description: Make model compilation selective. Currently 136 model files are all compiled. This phase adds CMake whitelist/blacklist so you build only what you need.
phases.principle: Model files (src/models/*.cpp) are independent compilation units. They register via a switch(arch) in llama-model.cpp. The CMake change globs the directory and filters. A runtime check provides a clear error if a model wasn't compiled.

create.content:
# Model architecture compilation
option(LLAMA_BUILD_ALL_MODELS "Build all model architectures" ON)
set(LLAMA_MODEL_WHITELIST "" CACHE STRING "Comma-separated model names (empty=all, e.g. 'gemma4,qwen3,phi3')")
set(LLAMA_MODEL_BLACKLIST "" CACHE STRING "Comma-separated model names to exclude")

file(GLOB MODEL_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/*.cpp")

# Apply whitelist
if(NOT LLAMA_BUILD_ALL_MODELS AND LLAMA_MODEL_WHITELIST)
    string(REPLACE "," ";" _whitelist "${LLAMA_MODEL_WHITELIST}")
    set(_filtered)
    foreach(_src ${MODEL_SOURCES})
        get_filename_component(_name ${_src} NAME_WE)
        if(_name IN_LIST _whitelist)
            list(APPEND _filtered ${_src})
        endif()
    endforeach()
    set(MODEL_SOURCES ${_filtered})
endif()

# Apply blacklist
if(LLAMA_MODEL_BLACKLIST)
    string(REPLACE "," ";" _blacklist "${LLAMA_MODEL_BLACKLIST}")
    foreach(_name ${_blacklist})
        list(FILTER MODEL_SOURCES EXCLUDE REGEX "${_name}\\.cpp$")
    endforeach()
endif()

# Generate compiled-archs list for runtime validation
set(_compiled_archs "")
foreach(_src ${MODEL_SOURCES})
    get_filename_component(_name ${_src} NAME_WE)
    list(APPEND _compiled_archs ${_name})
endforeach()
string(REPLACE ";" "," _compiled_archs_str "${_compiled_archs}")
configure_file(${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compiled-archs.h.in ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/compiled-archs.h @ONLY)

# Add to llama library target (assumes parent sets up the target)
set(LLAMA_MODEL_SOURCES ${MODEL_SOURCES} PARENT_SCOPE)
message(STATUS "Models: ${_compiled_archs_str} (${MODEL_SOURCES_COUNT} files)")

layer_adaptive_system.description: The TURBO_LAYER_ADAPTIVE env var controls per-layer quant type assignment during KV-cache construction. For weight quantization, a similar system assigns different weight quants per layer range (boundary layers get higher precision, middle layers get more compression).

modes.0: disabled — all layers use the same quant type
modes.1: boundary layers (first 4 + last 4) get Q8_0, rest get target type
modes.2: last 8 layers get Q8_0, rest get target type
modes.5: V-only: boundary layers get turbo4, rest get turbo2
modes.6: V-only: last 8 get turbo4, rest get turbo2
modes.7: V-only: boundary get Q8_0, rest get turbo2 (recommended)

layer_adaptive_system.for_weights: When quantizing model weights via the quantize tool, the same adaptive logic applies — boundary layers (which have outsized impact on output quality) get higher precision. This is already partially implemented in the kv-cache constructor; for weight quantization it needs to be applied in tools/quantize/quantize.cpp.

Perplexity check: build/bin/llama-perplexity -m model-tq3.gguf exits with PPL within 5% of F16 baseline

phases.name: port_stability_modules
phases.description: Port stability validation tooling AND quantization calibration system. The stability suite (PPL, KL divergence, round-trip) validates quant quality. The calibration suite (ported from ncnn's ncnn2table methodology) computes optimal activation scales to improve quantized model quality. This is the tool that makes PTQ quantization approach QAT quality.
what_needs_porting: STABILITY: KL divergence measurement between quantized and reference model logits
STABILITY: PPL+KLD test harness across model families
CALIBRATION: KL entropy calibrator (3-pass histogram → 128-bin fold → threshold sweep) — ncnn's default, highest accuracy
CALIBRATION: ACIQ analytic calibrator (single-pass Gaussian clip) — fast runtime recalibration
CALIBRATION: EQ cosine-similarity refinement (grid-search per-layer scales to maximize output cosine similarity) — accuracy maximizer
CALIBRATION: Activation scale table format (analogous to ncnn's .table but for GGUF per-layer per-tensor scales)
CALIBRATION: KV-cache activation calibrator (novel — ncnn doesn't calibrate KV; we extend the histogram/KL machinery to KV tensor collections)
CALIBRATION: Requantize fusion for chained quantized matmuls (propagate output scale = next layer input scale)

create.description: KL divergence computation between two logit distributions.
Implementation. Uses softmax normalization then element-wise KL formula. Handles temperature smoothing for numerical stability.
Quantization round-trip verification: quantize a weight tensor to a target type, dequantize back to F32, measure the reconstruction error.
Main test harness. Loads a reference model (F16) and a quantized model, runs the same prompt through both, compares PPL and KL divergence. Outputs a stability report.

create.content:
add_executable(llama-stability-runner
    stability_runner.cpp
    kl_divergence.cpp
    round_trip.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(llama-stability-runner PRIVATE llama llama-common)
install(TARGETS llama-stability-runner RUNTIME DESTINATION bin)

add_executable(llama-calibrate
    calibrator.cpp
    aciq.cpp
    kl_entropy.cpp
    eq_refine.cpp
    scale_table.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(llama-calibrate PRIVATE llama llama-common)
install(TARGETS llama-calibrate RUNTIME DESTINATION bin)

create.description: Core calibration API. Defines the calibration flow: collect activations from calibration data → compute scales → write scale table → optionally refine. Three algorithm choices mirror ncnn's ncnn2table -method flag.

KL entropy calibration — ncnn's default method (ncnn2table.cpp:604). Three-pass algorithm: (1) global absmax per activation tensor, (2) 2048-bin histogram, (3) threshold sweep with partial-bin linear interpolation. For each candidate threshold in [128, 2048], fold the clipped distribution into 128 bins, expand back, compute KL divergence, keep the minimizing threshold. Produces per-tensor activation scale = 127/best_threshold. Port from ncnn's quantize_KL function.
create.ncnn_reference: ncnn2table.cpp lines 604-1160: quantize_KL() function. The histogram fold logic (lines 1004-1070) is the core innovation — partial-bin linear interpolation when collapsing 2048 bins to 128.
create.llama_adaptation: Replace ncnn's conv_bottom_blobs with llama.cpp matmul input tensors (blk.{l}.attn_q.input, blk.{l}.ffn_gate.input, etc.). Activation collection uses llama_decode() with calibration prompts. Per-layer histograms stored per tensor name. LLM activations have heavier tails than CNN — consider 4096 bins instead of 2048 for better outlier modeling.

create.description: ACIQ (Analytic Clipping for Integer Quantization) — ncnn's fast method (ncnn2table.cpp:1206). Single-pass closed-form Gaussian clip. No histogram needed. Computes clip threshold from absmax + element count using the ACIQ alpha constant. Ideal for runtime recalibration when quantized model drifts.
create.ncnn_reference: ncnn2table.cpp lines 1206-1500: quantize_ACIQ() function. Formula: gaussian_const = 0.5*0.35*(1+sqrt(pi*ln4)), std = absmax*2*gaussian_const/sqrt(2*ln(N)), clip = alpha[7]*std = 3.92403714*std for int8.
create.llama_adaptation: Useful as a fast stability check during inference — if ACIQ-computed scales drift >10% from the calibration-time scales, trigger recalibration. The alpha constant for 4-bit quant (alpha[3]=1.185) differs from int8 — add a lookup table for all ggml quant types.

create.description: EQ (Entropy-aware Quantization) refinement — ncnn's accuracy maximizer (ncnn2table.cpp:1501). Seeds with KL or ACIQ scales, then grid-searches each per-layer scale to maximize cosine similarity between fp32 and quantized layer output. This is the calibration loop that gets closest to QAT quality.
create.ncnn_reference: ncnn2table.cpp lines 1501-1700: quantize_EQ() function. For each weight-scale channel and each activation scale, grid-search 100 steps over [0.5*scale, 2.0*scale], forward through standalone int8 layer, compare to fp32 reference, pick argmax cosine similarity.
create.llama_adaptation: Replace ncnn's standalone layer forward with llama.cpp's ggml_graph_compute with a single-layer subgraph. Measure cosine similarity between F16 and quantized output for each transformer layer independently. This is expensive (100 forwards per layer) but produces the highest-quality calibration.

create.description: Scale table serialization — read/write the calibration .table file. Analogous to ncnn's table format but using llama.cpp tensor naming conventions.

modify.instruction: Add KL divergence output mode. When run with --kl-reference <ref-model>, compute KL divergence between the reference and the model under test at each token position. Output mean/max/P95 KL alongside PPL.
modify.flag_to_add: --kl-reference <path> : compute KL divergence against this reference model

test_matrix.description: The PPL+KLD test harness evaluates each quant type across model families. This validates that modular quant additions don't regress quality.
metrics: PPL (perplexity) — lower is better, delta from F16 baseline
KL divergence (mean, max, P95) — lower is better
Round-trip cosine similarity — higher is better (1.0 = perfect)
TTFT (time to first token) — latency metric

calibration_methodology.source: Tencent/ncnn ncnn2table.cpp — ported and adapted for LLM/GGUF

two_scale_model.weight_scales: Per-output-channel (per-row for weight matrices). Computed from static weight absmax — no calibration data needed. Already partially present in llama.cpp k-quants (per-block scales). The calibration tool computes optimal per-channel scales instead of per-block.
two_scale_model.activation_scales: Per-tensor scalar for each matmul input tensor (attn_q.input, attn_k.input, ffn_gate.input, etc.). Requires calibration data. This is the novel contribution — llama.cpp currently has no activation scale calibration. ncnn's methodology ports directly.
two_scale_model.kv_cache_scales: Novel — ncnn doesn't calibrate KV cache. We extend the histogram/KL machinery to KV tensor activations. Per-layer per-tensor KV scale, computed from collected K/V activation samples during calibration. Enables KV-cache quant types (turbo/planar/iso) to use calibrated scales instead of naive absmax.

kl_entropy.accuracy: Highest among the three. TensorRT-standard entropy calibration.
kl_entropy.how_it_works: Pass 1: collect absmax per tensor. Pass 2: build 2048-bin histogram. Pass 3: for each threshold candidate [128..2048], fold distribution into 128 bins via partial-bin linear interpolation, expand back, compute KL(folded || expanded), pick minimum. Scale = 127/threshold.
kl_entropy.llama_adaptation: Replace ncnn conv_bottom_blobs with llama matmul input tensors. Use 4096 bins (not 2048) — LLM activations have heavier tails than CNNs. Forward calibration data through llama_decode(), extract intermediate activations per layer.

aciq.accuracy: Slightly lower than KL (~2-5% worse scale quality), but 3x faster to compute
aciq.how_it_works: Closed-form Gaussian assumption: clip = alpha[n_bits] * absmax * gaussian_const / sqrt(2*ln(N)). No histogram, no threshold sweep. Alpha constants from the ACIQ paper.
aciq.llama_adaptation: Ideal for runtime recalibration during inference. If the ACIQ-computed scale for the current batch drifts >10% from the calibration-time scale, trigger an online scale update. This is the stability monitor's fast path.

eq_refine.accuracy: Highest overall. Grid-searches each scale to maximize output cosine similarity. Gets closest to QAT quality from pure PTQ.
eq_refine.how_it_works: Seed with KL or ACIQ scales. For each layer: for each candidate scale in [0.5x, 2.0x] (100 steps), quantize that layer, forward 50 calibration samples, measure cosine similarity between F16 and quantized output. Pick argmax.
eq_refine.llama_adaptation: The single most valuable calibration algorithm for our use case. Apply per-transformer-layer (not per-tensor). This recovers most of the quality gap between PTQ and QAT for turbo/planar/iso KV-cache quant types.

requantize_fusion.description: When two consecutive matmuls are both quantized, propagate the first layer's output scale to match the second layer's input scale. Eliminates a dequant→requant round-trip.
requantize_fusion.llama_adaptation: Apply to chained transformer matmuls: attn_q→attn_output, ffn_gate→ffn_down. The fusion sets output_scale[layer_l] = input_scale[layer_l+1] so the requantize happens inline during the matmul output write.

recommended_workflow: 1. Run KL entropy calibration on 500 calibration samples → produces initial scale table
2. Run EQ refinement on the KL-seeded table → refines scales to maximize cosine similarity
3. Quantize model with refined scales: llama-calibrate --model model.gguf --calibrate data.txt --method eq --output model.table
4. Apply: llama-quantize --scales model.table --type Q4_K model.gguf model-q4.gguf
6. Runtime: ACIQ monitor checks for distribution drift during inference, triggers recalibration if needed

validation: cmake --build build -j$(nproc) exits 0
build/bin/llama-stability-runner --help exits 0
build/bin/llama-calibrate --help exits 0
Round-trip test: round_trip_test with Q4_0 returns cos_sim > 0.99
KL divergence: kl_divergence on identical distributions returns ~0.0
Full stability run: stability-runner --ref model-f16.gguf --quant model-q4.gguf produces report with all metrics
KL calibration: llama-calibrate --model model.gguf --method kl --calibrate data.txt --output model.table produces non-empty scale table
ACIQ calibration: llama-calibrate --method aciq completes in <30s for a 7B model
EQ refinement: llama-calibrate --method eq produces scales with cos_sim > 0.99 per layer
Scale application: llama-quantize --scales model.table produces model with PPL 2-5% better than without scales

phases.name: hybrid_backend_skeleton
phases.description: Create the ggml-hybrid backend — a first-class ggml_backend_i implementation that simultaneously dispatches to CPU threads (AVX2/AVX-512/NEON) and iGPU compute (Vulkan). From the scheduler's perspective it's one backend. Internally it splits GEMM rows across CPU and iGPU with zero synchronization.
phases.principle: The hybrid backend exploits Unified Memory Architecture (UMA) on laptops/edge devices where CPU and iGPU share the same physical RAM. Unlike discrete GPU backends (CUDA, Metal) which require PCIe data transfers, the hybrid backend reads/writes the same memory pages from both units. This mirrors cactus-kernels' zero-copy philosophy.
phases.scope: Targets: Intel Iris Xe, AMD Radeon iGPU (APU), Apple Silicon (via Metal unified memory), ARM Mali/Adreno. Not for discrete GPUs (those use CUDA/Vulkan backends directly).

create.content:
option(GGML_HYBRID "ggml: use hybrid CPU+iGPU backend" OFF)

if(GGML_HYBRID)
    message(STATUS "Hybrid CPU+iGPU backend enabled")
    set(HYBRID_SOURCES
        ggml-hybrid.cpp
        uma/uma-buffer.cpp
        compute/mul-mat-dispatch.cpp
        compute/dequant-vulkan.cpp
        scheduler/thermal-balancer.cpp
    )

    # Require Vulkan for iGPU compute
    find_package(Vulkan REQUIRED)

    # GLSL compute shaders compiled to SPIR-V at build time
    file(GLOB HYBRID_SHADERS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/shaders/*.comp")
    foreach(shader ${HYBRID_SHADERS})
        get_filename_component(shader_name ${shader} NAME_WE)
        # Embed SPIR-V as C header (glslangValidator or glslc)
        add_custom_command(
            OUTPUT ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${shader_name}.spv.h
            COMMAND ${Vulkan_GLSLANG_VALIDATOR} -V --vn ${shader_name}_spv
                    -o ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${shader_name}.spv.h ${shader}
            DEPENDS ${shader}
        )
        list(APPEND HYBRID_SOURCES ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${shader_name}.spv.h)
    endforeach()

    add_library(ggml-hybrid OBJECT ${HYBRID_SOURCES})
    target_link_libraries(ggml-hybrid PUBLIC Vulkan::Vulkan)
    target_include_directories(ggml-hybrid PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})
endif()

create.description: Zero-copy UMA buffer allocation. Allocates system RAM that is simultaneously accessible by CPU (via pointer) and iGPU (via Vulkan memory mapping). On Linux uses VK_EXT_external_memory_host or DMA-BUF. On Windows uses ReBAR. Eliminates all data transfers between CPU and iGPU.

The core GEMM dispatcher. Splits the output tensor dst into two disjoint row ranges: CPU writes [0..split_row), iGPU writes [split_row..N). No synchronization between them because the memory regions don't overlap.
PID controller that measures CPU vs iGPU completion time per transformer layer and adjusts the split ratio. Prevents thermal throttling from causing one unit to idle while waiting for the other.

backend_registration.description: The hybrid backend registers quant support for types that have Vulkan dequant shaders. Types without shaders fall back to CPU (still within the hybrid backend — the CPU thread pool handles them).

validation: cmake -B build -DGGML_HYBRID=ON -DGGML_VULKAN=ON exits 0
cmake --build build -j$(nproc) exits 0
ggml_backend_hybrid_is_uma() returns true on Intel/AMD iGPU systems
Loading a model with hybrid backend: CPU utilization + iGPU utilization both > 0
Adaptive balancer adjusts split ratio over time (log shows cpu_ratio changing)

phases.name: hybrid_uma_tensor_slicing
phases.description: Implement the disjoint UMA tensor slicing for GEMM operations. The CPU and iGPU write to non-overlapping rows of the same output tensor — zero synchronization, zero data copy.
phases.principle: Standard CPU+GPU split requires a sync barrier after the split because both units might write to overlapping memory. Disjoint slicing eliminates this by giving each unit a strictly non-overlapping row range in the output tensor. Since they share UMA RAM, both read the same src0 (weights) and src1 (activations) without copying.
phases.key_constraint: src0 (weights) and src1 (activations) are READ-ONLY by both units — safe to share. dst (output) is split into disjoint regions — safe to write concurrently. The only synchronization is waiting for BOTH to finish before the NEXT graph operation (handled by ggml's graph scheduler, not by the hybrid backend).

create.description: Full implementation of hybrid_mul_mat_dispatch. Creates tensor views for CPU and iGPU slices, launches both concurrently, waits for both at the end.
create.key_detail: Creating a tensor view is zero-copy pointer arithmetic: igpu_view.data = (char*)dst->data + split_row * dst->nb[1]. No allocation, no copy.

ops_to_dispatch: GGML_OP_MUL_MAT — primary target (GEMM is 80%+ of transformer compute)
GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID — MoE expert dispatch (same row-split pattern)
Other ops fall through to CPU-only (iGPU acceleration not worth the overhead)
validation: GEMM correctness: output matches CPU-only reference for all split ratios [0.1 .. 0.9]
No race conditions: valgrind/helgrind clean on the output tensor
Performance: hybrid GEMM latency < max(cpu_only, igpu_only) for balanced split

phases.name: hybrid_vulkan_dequant_shaders
phases.description: Write Vulkan compute shaders that dequantize ggml quant types directly in the iGPU shader using subgroup operations. This keeps weights compressed in shared RAM while computing in FP16/FP32 — minimizing memory bandwidth pressure, which is the critical bottleneck on edge devices.
phases.principle: cactus-kernels achieves high performance on ARM via hand-tuned NEON SIMD intrinsics. The iGPU equivalent is Vulkan Subgroups (GL_KHR_shader_subgroup_*). 32 iGPU threads cooperatively dequantize a 256-element block in a single clock cycle using subgroup shuffles to broadcast scales across the wavefront.

create.description: Vulkan GLSL compute shader for Q4_0 matrix multiplication with inline dequantization. Uses subgroup shuffle for block-scale broadcast and subgroupAdd for warp-level reduction.
Q4_K variant — more complex block structure (super-blocks with 8 sub-scales). Uses 2 subgroup shuffles per super-block.
Turbo3 variant — dequantizes WHT-rotated Q2 blocks. Uses subgroup matrix multiply for the 4x4 Hadamard step.
Q8_0 variant — simplest (8-bit symmetric). Baseline for performance comparison.

quant_caps_integration.description: After writing each shader, register the type as supported on the hybrid backend via ggml_backend_register_quant_ops(). The caps table (Phase 2) already knows the type's semantic capabilities — the hybrid backend just declares it has a kernel for it.

validation: Each shader compiles via glslangValidator without errors
Q4_0 GEMM output matches CPU reference within fp32 epsilon
Q4_K GEMM output matches CPU reference
iGPU shader execution time < CPU-only execution time for K >= 1024 (bandwidth-bound regime)

phases.name: hybrid_adaptive_thermal_balancer
phases.description: Implement the PID controller that dynamically adjusts CPU/iGPU workload split based on completion time deltas and thermal telemetry. Prevents either unit from idling while the other throttles.
phases.principle: Edge devices aggressively throttle under sustained AI loads. If the iGPU hits 85C, its clock halves, making it slower than the CPU. A static 50/50 split would cause the CPU to finish early and idle. The adaptive balancer measures per-layer completion times and shifts the split ratio to keep both units busy.

macos: powermetrics — SMC thermal/power (requires sudo, sampled at 1s intervals)
windows: Intel Power Gadget API — CPU power/freq
telemetry_sources.fallback: If no thermal telemetry available, use completion-time-only PID (no thermal override).

validation: Under sustained load: cpu_ratio converges (oscillation dampens within 20 layers)
Thermal throttle simulation: forcing igpu_temp > 85 causes ratio to shift toward CPU
Cold start: ratio starts at 0.5 and adapts within 5 layers
No telemetry: defaults to fixed 0.5 split with warning log

phases.name: hybrid_prober_integration
phases.description: Add the hybrid backend to llama_prober_config.json so it auto-detects on Intel/AMD iGPU systems. No flags needed — if an iGPU with UMA is detected, the hybrid backend is enabled alongside Vulkan.

modify.instruction: Add a new probe entry for the hybrid backend. It should detect Intel/AMD integrated graphics (NOT discrete NVIDIA/AMD dGPUs — those use CUDA/HIP directly). The probe checks for: (1) iGPU hardware via lspci, (2) UMA capability via Vulkan memory properties, (3) Vulkan SDK availability.

entry_to_add.notes: The hybrid backend requires Vulkan for iGPU compute. If iGPU detected but no UMA, falls back to Vulkan-only (CPU+iGPU with copy overhead). If no iGPU, falls back to CPU+BLAS.

modify.instruction: Add UMA capability check. After detecting an iGPU, verify it shares system RAM (UMA). If not UMA (discrete GPU masquerading as integrated), skip hybrid — use the dedicated backend instead.

validation: On Intel Iris Xe laptop: cmake -B build auto-enables GGML_HYBRID=ON + GGML_VULKAN=ON
On NVIDIA dGPU desktop: hybrid NOT enabled (lspci doesn't match integrated pattern)
On CPU-only server: hybrid NOT enabled, CPU+BLAS used
cmake --build build -j$(nproc) exits 0 with hybrid enabled

phases.name: integrate_stq1_0
phases.description: Integrate STQ1_0 (1.31 bpw structured ternary) from Tencent AngelSlim PR #22836. STQ1_0 is the RUNTIME INFERENCE FORMAT for the Sherry quantization algorithm (arxiv.org/abs/2601.07892). Sherry introduces 3:4 fine-grained sparsity — exactly one zero per group of 4 weights — achieving 1.25-bit width with power-of-two alignment. STQ1_0 stores these weights in 5 bits per group (1.31 bpw including fp16 scale). Includes ARM NEON optimized dot product using codebook table lookup + vdotq. Ideal for extreme edge-device compression.

relationship_to_sherry.sherry: The TRAINING algorithm (Python/PyTorch). Produces STQ1_0-formatted weights via QAT with 'Arenas' annealing to prevent weight trapping. Not portable to C — stays as external tool.
relationship_to_sherry.stq1_0: The RUNTIME FORMAT (C/ggml). Stores and computes Sherry-trained weights at inference time. This is what Phase 18 integrates.
relationship_to_sherry.summary: Phase 18 = inference kernel. Use pre-trained Sherry weights from AngelSlim's HuggingFace (e.g., HY-1.8B-2Bit, Hy-MT1.5-1.8B-1.25bit). Do NOT expect PTQ (post-training quantization via llama-quantize) to match paper quality — the 3:4 sparsity pattern must be learned during training.

qat_trained.result: Zero accuracy loss vs SOTA ternary across 5 benchmarks (ARC, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, MMLU)
qat_trained.speedup: 10% faster than 2-bit ternary on Intel i7-14700HX CPU (due to 25% fewer bits)
qat_trained.note: These results require QAT-trained weights from Sherry's Python framework

ptq_estimated.model: Any model quantized via llama-quantize --type STQ1_0
ptq_estimated.reason: The structured 3:4 sparsity pattern (exactly one zero per group of 4) is suboptimal when applied post-hoc. Sherry's QAT learns which weight to zero per group — PTQ picks the smallest, which is a greedy heuristic that leaves quality on the table.
ptq_estimated.recommendation: Use STQ1_0 PTQ only for rapid prototyping. For production, use pre-trained Sherry weights from HuggingFace.

quality_benchmarks.compression_ratio: 1.31 bpw = 8.2% of F16 model size. A 7B model: F16=14GB → STQ1_0=1.15GB.

phases.source_diff: Full diff retrieved and analyzed. The PR touches 16 files across ggml, CPU backend, and llama tools.

pr_summary.block: block_stq1_0: qs[QK_K/8] (4-bit code) + sign[QK_K/32] (1-bit table select) + d (fp16 scale)
pr_summary.codebook: 32-entry lookup table: (sign<<4 | slot) -> packed 4-lane ternary pattern. Reverse maps: 256-entry qpack->slot and qpack->sign for encoding.

kernels.arm_neon: ggml_vec_dot_stq1_0_q8_K in ggml-cpu/arch/arm/quants.c (NEON + DOTPROD, 32-byte tbl lookup + vdotq)
kernels.arch_fallbacks: Added to all arch files: arm, x86, riscv, powerpc, s390x, loongarch

pr_summary.use_case: Weight quantization for extreme compression on edge devices. Not suitable for KV cache (too low precision for attention).

adaptation_for_turboquant.problem: The PR is against upstream llama.cpp master (GGML_TYPE_COUNT=42). The turboquant branch has TURBO types at values 37-40 and will have PLANAR/ISO at 47-50. STQ1_0's enum value 42 may conflict.
adaptation_for_turboquant.solution: Assign STQ1_0 the next available value AFTER all turboquant/planar/iso types. If GGML_TYPE_COUNT is already 51 (after planar/iso port in Phase 8), assign STQ1_0=51 and increment GGML_TYPE_COUNT=52.
adaptation_for_turboquant.type_traits: Append entry after the last custom type in the type_traits[] array
adaptation_for_turboquant.dispatch: Append case in the quantize_chunk switch after the last custom type

files_to_modify.action: Add GGML_TYPE_STQ1_0 = <next_available_value> before GGML_TYPE_COUNT. Increment GGML_TYPE_COUNT.
Add block_stq1_0 struct after block_tq2_0. Add codebook tables (stq1_0_codebook[32], stq1_0_qpack_to_slot[256], stq1_0_qpack_to_sign[256]) inside GGML_COMMON_IMPL guard.
files_to_modify.from_pr: block struct + 3 GGML_TABLE_BEGIN blocks. Copy verbatim — these are mathematical constants, not branch-dependent.

files_to_modify.action: Add declarations: quantize_row_stq1_0_ref, dequantize_row_stq1_0, quantize_stq1_0. Append after tq2_0 declarations.

Add implementations: quantize_row_stq1_0_ref (encoder using reverse codebook maps), dequantize_row_stq1_0 (decoder using forward codebook), quantize_stq1_0 (wrapper). Add ggml_validate_row_data case. Append after tq2_0 implementations.
files_to_modify.from_pr: quantize_row_stq1_0_ref (~55 lines), dequantize_row_stq1_0 (~30 lines), quantize_stq1_0 (~6 lines), validate case (~3 lines)

files_to_modify.action: Add: quantize_row_stq1_0 declaration, ggml_vec_dot_stq1_0_q8_K declaration, ggml_vec_dot_stq1_0_q8_K_generic declaration.
Add quantize_row_stq1_0 wrapper + ggml_vec_dot_stq1_0_q8_K_generic (scalar reference dot product). Copy verbatim from PR.

Add ggml_vec_dot_stq1_0_q8_K (ARM NEON optimized). This is the performance-critical kernel — uses vqtbl2q + vdotq for codebook lookup and dot product in a single pass. Copy verbatim from PR (~110 lines).
files_to_modify.note: If building for x86-only, this file is not compiled. The arch-fallback.h provides the generic mapping.

files_to_modify.action: Add #define ggml_vec_dot_stq1_0_q8_K_generic to all arch sections (6 locations). Copy verbatim from PR.
Add GGML_TYPE_STQ1_0 to 6 switch cases: compute_forward_add, add1, acc, out_prod, set, get_rows, clamp. Each is a 1-line append next to existing TQ1_0/TQ2_0 entries.
Add type_traits[GGML_TYPE_STQ1_0] entry (type_name, blck_size=QK_K, type_size=sizeof(block_stq1_0), is_quantized=true, to_float, from_float_ref). Add quantize_chunk dispatch case.
Add caps entry: [GGML_TYPE_STQ1_0] = { .weight_capable=true, .cpu_fallback_ok=true }. STQ1_0 is weight-only — no needs_wht, no needs_deferred, no KV-cache capability.
Add LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_STQ1_0 = <next_available> to the ftype enum.
Add ftype name string ('STQ1_0 - 1.31 bpw ternary') and GGML_TYPE_STQ1_0 -> LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_STQ1_0 mapping.
Add STQ1_0 to tensor_type_fallback and llama_ftype_get_default_type. Add to the TQ1_0/TQ2_0 fallback group (these extreme low-bit types fall back to Q4_K for 1d tensors).
Add { 'STQ1_0', LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_STQ1_0, ' 1.31 bpw ternarization' } to QUANT_OPTIONS.
Add STQ1_0 to test error thresholds (uses MAX_QUANTIZATION_TOTAL_ERROR_BINARY and MAX_DOT_PRODUCT_ERROR_BINARY, same as Q1_0).
Add STQ1_0=42 to GGMLQuantizationType enum, MOSTLY_STQ1_0 to LlamaFileType, and block size mapping (256, 42).

hybrid_integration.description: After integration, add a Vulkan compute shader for STQ1_0 in the hybrid backend (Phase 15 pattern). The codebook lookup translates perfectly to Vulkan subgroup shuffle — 32 threads cooperatively decode one 4-lane group.
hybrid_integration.shader_plan: ggml/src/ggml-hybrid/shaders/gemm_stq1_0.comp — uses stq1_0_codebook as a uniform buffer, subgroupShuffle to broadcast the codebook index, and subgroupAdd for the dot-product reduction.

phases.name: port_tequila_ternary
phases.description: Port the Tequila ternary quantization algorithm from Tencent AngelSlim. Tequila solves 'deadzone trapping' — a failure mode where weights stuck at the zero boundary receive only noisy gradients during training, collapsing model capacity. Tequila repurposes trapped weights as dynamic biases that receive meaningful gradients. Paper: arxiv.org/abs/2509.23809. Tequila is a QAT algorithm; the C port implements the quantize/dequantize runtime format and an improved PTQ quantizer that approximates the deadzone fix.
phases.source_language: Python (PyTorch) — quantizer ported to C, training stays Python
phases.what_to_port: The core quantization algorithm: deadzone-aware ternary rounding. For each weight block, compute the optimal ternary mapping {-1, 0, +1} with an adaptive threshold that accounts for the deadzone boundary. The PTQ approximation: instead of retraining trapped weights (which requires QAT), apply a correction bias to weights near the deadzone boundary, partially recovering the quality gap.
phases.difference_from_stq1_0: STQ1_0 forces structured sparsity (exactly one zero per 4 lanes, Sherry format). Tequila is unstructured ternary — each weight independently maps to {-d, 0, +d}. Tequila achieves higher quality (2.0 bpw vs 1.31 bpw) because unstructured ternary has more representational freedom. The deadzone correction helps even in PTQ mode.

qat_trained.ARC: >4% accuracy gain over SOTA ternary baseline (e.g., TWN, BitNet)
qat_trained.vs_full_precision: <1% accuracy gap on ARC (nearly matching F16)
qat_trained.5benchmark_avg: Best ternary SOTA across ARC, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, MMLU
qat_trained.speedup: 3.0x inference speedup vs F16 (ternary replaces multiply with add)

ptq_estimated.model: Any model quantized via llama-quantize --type TEQUILA
ptq_estimated.estimated_quality: ~85-90% of F16 accuracy (better than STQ1_0 PTQ because deadzone correction helps even without QAT)
ptq_estimated.reason: The deadzone bias correction partially mitigates the trapping issue even in PTQ. Weights near zero get a small correction term that pushes them to the correct side of the boundary, recovering some of the capacity loss.
ptq_estimated.vs_tq2_0: Expected to match or slightly beat TQ2_0 (2.06 bpw) quality at similar compression, because Tequila's deadzone fix addresses TQ2_0's main quality bottleneck.

quality_benchmarks.compression_ratio: 2.0 bpw = 12.5% of F16 model size. A 7B model: F16=14GB → TEQUILA=1.75GB.

new_type.block: block_tequila: q[QK_K/4] (2-bit codes: 00=-1, 01=0, 10=+1) + d (fp16 scale) + imatrix_scale (fp16 per-block importance weight). Block size QK_K=256, sizeof = sizeof(ggml_half)*2 + QK_K/4 = 68 bytes → 2.125 bpw.

create.description: Tequila ternary quantization implementation. Port from Python reference: quantize_row_tequila_ref (optimal ternary with imatrix weighting), dequantize_row_tequila, quantize_tequila (wrapper). The key algorithm: for each block of 256 weights, compute the optimal threshold for mapping to {-1, 0, +1} weighted by the importance matrix.

modify: Same 16-file pattern as Phase 18 (STQ1_0): enum, block struct, declarations, implementations, type_traits, dispatch case, ops.cpp cases, ftype, quantize tool, tests, caps entry

imatrix_integration.description: Tequila uses the importance matrix to guide quantization. The imatrix provides per-block sensitivity weights. Blocks with high importance get more careful rounding (prefer 0 over +/-1 when close to threshold). This requires the quantize tool to pass the imatrix to the quantization function.
imatrix_integration.api: quantize_tequila(src, dst, nrows, n_per_row, imatrix) — the imatrix parameter is already supported in the ggml quantize API (used by Q4_K, IQ series).

phases.name: port_angelslim_algorithms
phases.description: Catalog of additional algorithms from Tencent AngelSlim. STQ1_0 (Phase 18) already provides the runtime format for Sherry weights. This phase covers the remaining algorithms: LeptoQuant (FP8 calibration tool), DAQ (Python-only, not portable), and Eagle3 (speculative decoding). Each is assessed for portability and quality.

compression_vs_quality.note: AngelSlim benchmarks: Qwen3-8B FP8-Static CEVAL 78.23 vs BF16 79.27 (-1.3%)
<1% gap on ARC vs F16. Best ternary SOTA.
Current turboquant. Quality ceiling for pure PTQ ternary.
Zero loss vs SOTA ternary. 25% fewer bits than 2-bit.
Degraded without QAT. Use pre-trained Sherry weights for production.
Baseline binary. Too lossy for most models.

quality_landscape.key_insight: The quality gap between QAT and PTQ widens dramatically below 3 bpw. At 4+ bpw, PTQ (GPTQ/AWQ) nearly matches F16. At 2 bpw, QAT (Tequila) is ~7% better than PTQ (TQ2_0). At 1.31 bpw, QAT (Sherry) is ~10-15% better than PTQ (STQ1_0). Conclusion: for extreme compression (<3 bpw), use pre-trained QAT weights. For moderate compression (4+ bpw), PTQ is sufficient.

algorithms.name: Sherry (training algorithm — runtime format already in Phase 18)
algorithms.description: STQ1_0 (Phase 18) is the runtime inference format for Sherry weights. The Sherry training algorithm itself stays in Python (requires PyTorch autograd for Arenas annealing). To get Sherry-quality weights, use AngelSlim's pre-trained models from HuggingFace.
algorithms.runtime_status: ALREADY INTEGRATED as STQ1_0 in Phase 18. No separate runtime work needed.
algorithms.training_status: Python-only. Not portable to C. Use external tool + pre-trained weights.
algorithms.quality_qat: Zero accuracy loss vs SOTA ternary on LLaMA-3.2 1B (5 benchmarks). <2% gap from F16.
algorithms.quality_ptq: ~80-85% of F16 (greedy heuristic, no Arenas annealing). Not recommended for production.

algorithms.name: LeptoQuant
algorithms.description: FP8 quantization with KL-divergence-minimizing scale calibration. The ggml FP8 type (GGML_TYPE_F8_E4M3) already exists upstream — LeptoQuant adds the calibration step that computes optimal per-tensor/per-channel scales.
algorithms.approach: Port the calibration tool to tools/quantize/. No new ggml type needed. The tool reads a model + calibration data, computes FP8 scales that minimize KL divergence, and writes a quantized GGUF.
algorithms.port_effort: Low — quant type exists, just calibration math

quality.note: FP8 is the sweet spot: <2% quality loss, 2x compression, native hardware support on H100/RTX 4090

algorithms.name: DAQ (Distribution-Aware Quantization)
algorithms.description: DAQ preserves knowledge distribution during post-training training updates. Uses distillation-style loss to keep quantized model's output close to original. Requires calibration data + iterative optimization.
algorithms.approach: Not portable to C runtime — requires iterative weight updates (training). Keep as external Python tool that produces calibrated GGUF files.
algorithms.quality: Preserves knowledge during fine-tuning of already-quantized models. Niche use case.

algorithms.name: Eagle3 (Speculative Decoding)
algorithms.description: Eagle3 trains a small drafter model that reads the target model's hidden state and speculates multiple tokens. Achieves 1.4-1.9x speedup with accept length 1.8-3.5.

quality.note: Eagle3 is orthogonal to quantization — works with any quant type. Combines well with KV-cache quantization (turbo/planar) for maximum throughput.

algorithms.integration: Uses llama_get_hidden_state() API from Phase 10. Drafter model is a separate GGUF in a second llama_context linked via ctx_other. Training is external (AngelSlim provides pre-trained drafter weights on HuggingFace for Qwen3, Hunyuan, etc.).
algorithms.port_effort: Low for inference — hidden state API + speculative decode already exist. Medium for training (external Python tool).
